class_name: 疑問-問いかけ-モノカ類

provenance.pipeline: satsuki v1: author → mechanical attachment gate → cold review → fixes applied → gate re-run

patterns.usage_note: Denies a state rather than an act: put as a question, 痛いもんか says it does not hurt in the slightest and うまいもんか says the food is nothing of the sort. The corpus licenses it after a plain adjective (and after past た/だ), which is what separates it from the verb-attaching もんか of the ハズガナイ group, where 二度と行くもんか is a vow of refusal rather than a verdict on how things are. It is the colloquial contraction of ものか and sounds rough and emphatic, so it stays out of formal settings and away from superiors; ものですか / もんですか are the politer variants and are more associated with female speakers.

examples.ruby: このくらいのかすり傷[きず]が痛[いた]いもんか。
examples.english: A scratch this size? It doesn't hurt one bit.

examples.ruby: 十月[じゅうがつ]の海[うみ]がそんなに冷[つめ]たいもんか。
examples.english: As if the sea in October is that cold.

examples.ruby: あんな作[つく]り話[ばなし]の映画[えいが]が怖[こわ]いもんか。
examples.english: A movie that made-up? As if it could be scary.
